initiative: Biology and Therapeutic Development for Cutaneous Neurofibromas
summary: Biology and Therapeutic Development for Cutaneous Neurofibroma (BTD cNF) initiative aims to accelerate the next era of discovery and therapeutics to prevent and treat cNF patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). The focus areas of this initiative are i) understand the cNF development process, ii) identify and validate therapeutic candidates for cNF, iii) identify and validate non-invasive approaches in humans and preclinical systems for detection of cNF change, iv) define or validate key variables and endpoints for cNF clinical trials, and v) develop the infrastructure for cNF clinical trials. There are a total of 9 laboratories around the globe funded as part of this initiative.

The Brain Tumor Initiative (BTI), funded by Gilbert Family Foundation focuses on identifying and developing therapeutic strategies to effectively treat neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated transformed gliomas (non-optical pathway gliomas). BTI is conducting clinical studies to provide critical characterization of NF1 high grade glioma and identify the most promising treatments for patients available today. BTI also invests in preclinical research tools to help drug discovery and development.

The Cell Culture Initiative, funded by Neurofibromatosis Therapeutic Acceleration Program, addresses the lack of cellular culture models, and aims to provide a rapid, cost effective way to predict the efficacy of potential drug candidates alone and in combination.

Cutaneous Neurofibroma (cNF) Initiative, funded by Neurofibromatosis Therapeutic Acceleration Program, spurs the highest priority research for cNFs, which are often identified by NF1 patients as their greatest burden. This initiative brings together multi-disciplinary perspectives to understand and treat cNF.
